terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.method: homography from the black border rule's four fitted edge lines (homography.json)
referenceCamera.note: Not solved with solve_camera_pose.py, which had nothing to fit: this subject is planar, so the camera IS a homography and the plate gives it exactly. The diamond's two diagonals must be equal and measure 333/413 px, so the plate is seen acos(0.806) = 36.3 deg off its normal. The -8 deg roll is the plate's in-plane tilt in the photograph, confirmed independently by the left vertex's two edge slopes (0.94 and 0.66, mean 0.80 = cos 36.3). Camera framing only - neither the yaw nor the roll is modelled into the prop, which stands square and faces +Z.

objectClass.notes: The pictogram DEPICTS an animal; the object is not one. primaryDomain stays 'object' and no anatomy track runs - the elephant exists only as a 2D filled silhouette drawn into a canvas, where getting it right is a draughting problem, not an anatomy one. Nothing on this prop moves: no hinge, no bearing, no fastening that a game articulates.

reasoning: GEOMETRICALLY this is near the simple end: two extruded rounded profiles and a square prism, measured at ~150 triangles against an 800 ceiling. Triangles are not the constraint here.

It is NOT rated simple because localDetailDensity is 7: the whole identity of the prop lives in printed detail - the pictogram, two border rules, two lines of legend in two scripts, four fasteners and a weathering gradient. Rating it simple would set targetMinDetails low enough to let the pictogram through as 'a black shape', which is the one thing that would make the prop read as a generic yellow diamond instead of an elephant crossing sign.
actionReadinessNeed 1: a sealed static sign. One root pivot, no sockets, no destruction groups.
occlusionRisk 2: only the plate backs and the post behind the diamond are unseen, and both are plain surfaces whose treatment follows from the visible edge return.
complexity.scoreNote: Scores are the validator's 0-3 scale. localDetailDensity is at the CEILING of 3 and everything else is at or below 1: that asymmetry IS this prop. Its geometry is two extruded profiles and a prism; its identity is a printed pictogram and two lines of legend.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Two macro components is not a shallow tree here, it is the DESIGNED answer to a maxDrawCalls of 2. One component is one draw call, so the plates must share a mesh; the meso level (diamond plate, supplementary plate, edge return) is carried inside that one component's geometryDescriptor rather than as separate components, and that is recorded explicitly so a later pass does not 'fix' the shallow tree by splitting it and silently doubling the prop's cost in every scene. repetitionSystems: none - the four fasteners are the only repeated part and they are below the resolvable threshold at prop distance, so they go in the canvas, not into an InstancedMesh that would spend a draw call the prop does not have. localOverrides ARE needed: the algal staining at the plate margins and the rust at the post base are bounded regions of a different colour on an otherwise uniform surface.

detailInventory.scanMethod: grid-3x3 zones, then per-detail re-crop at 512 px (crops/*.jpg)
detailInventory.note: Eleven details against a raised target of 8. Nine of the eleven are PRINTED, not modelled: this prop's identity lives almost entirely in the legend canvas, and the geometry it hangs on is two extruded profiles and a prism. The two that are geometry - the corner radius and the edge return - are both on the SILHOUETTE, which is exactly where a texture cannot help.

details.description: Solid black filled elephant silhouette, walking, FACING -X (the viewer's left). Domed head, small rounded Asian-elephant ear, trunk hanging and hooking forward at the tip, two short tusks curving forward, four legs in a walking stagger with the near foreleg planted forward, thin tail with a tuft. Painted decal technique, not an engraved groove and not a contour: the reference shows a hard colour boundary with zero relief and zero shadow inside it. Drawn as SOLID FILL, never an outline - that is what lets it survive both highway distance and a low texture resolution.

Black rule inset from the diamond outline, following the same rounded-corner path. Measured stroke 14/11/13 px on three scans, which is a 45-deg crossing of the edge: perpendicular stroke 9 px = 0.020 m. Edge-to-rule margin 0.014 m. Painted line, no relief - the reference shows a hard colour boundary and no shadow along it.

The same black rule inset from the supplementary plate's rounded rectangle outline. Measured 3 px stroke = 0.007 m with an 0.011 m margin, both at the measurement floor of a 1024 plate; confidence is correspondingly low and the stroke is drawn proportional to the diamond's rather than trusted absolutely.

Upper legend line, Thai script: ระวังช้าง. Set noticeably larger than the English line and with the tall tone marks and the ช ascender clearing the cap line. Redrawn from the correct string rather than traced from the plate's glyphs, which came from a fast image model.

Lower legend line, ELEPHANT CROSSING, all caps, CONDENSED - measured per-glyph advance is about 0.55 of cap height, so a normal-width face set at the same size overruns the plate. Letter-spaced to fill the plate width between the border rule margins.

Two dark round bolt heads per plate, on the plate's vertical centreline near the top and bottom margins - four in total, each ~4 px = 0.009 m. Deliberately NOT an InstancedMesh: at prop distance they are sub-pixel, and an instanced system would spend a draw call on a prop whose ceiling is 2. Drawn into the legend canvas as dark discs with a light rim. Recorded as `linework` (painted decal) rather than `fastener`: the taxonomy's `fastener` kind is a contract to build an instanced system and the validator enforces exactly that, so claiming it would promise a system that does not exist. What is built is a decal - colour contrast, no relief - which is what `linework` names.
details.kindNote: Reclassified from `fastener` deliberately. At 0.009 m these are sub-pixel at prop distance, and an InstancedMesh would spend one of only two draw calls to say so.

details.description: Both plates carry rounded corners on their outline. Measured on the diamond by extrapolating each vertex's two straight edges to their intersection and taking the apex setback: left vertex 0.044 m, top vertex 0.031 m, adopted 0.038 m. The supplementary plate reads ~0.025 m. REAL GEOMETRY, carried in the extrusion profile: a square-cornered plate reads as a hazard board rather than a road sign, and the rounding is on the SILHOUETTE, where no texture can put it.

The plate is folded sheet, not a flat cut panel: a grey edge return runs the full outline, visible along the diamond's upper-right side because the camera sits ~36 deg off the face normal. Given real depth (0.006 m) plus a small extrusion bevel so the rim catches a grazing highlight instead of reading as a zero-thickness card. This is also why the plate front and back are not the same colour.

Desaturated yellow-green weathering (~#93A03C) concentrated on the diamond's outboard margin and along the fold, i.e. where water sits, and absent from the middle of the face. A bounded region of a different albedo on an otherwise uniform surface - a localOverride, not a global material change.

Vertical mid-value orange-brown streaks (~#8A5330) running down the post from roughly the supplementary plate's fixing downward, widening into a solid band at the cut end. Runoff from the fixings, so it starts AT a fixing and runs down - a streak that starts in mid-air reads wrong.

A single vertical arris runs the full visible length of the post with a lit face either side of it, and the cut end reads square. Real geometry - the corner of a square hollow section - not a painted seam. It is the evidence the post is SHS rather than a U-channel, and the reason the post is a square prism rather than a cylinder despite the declared cylinder COLLIDER.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
qualityContract.minimumSpecDepthNote: mesoComponents is 0 BY DESIGN, and it is the one number in this contract that was lowered rather than met. The prop does have three meso parts - the diamond plate, the supplementary plate and the edge return - and they are named, dimensioned and evidenced in componentTree[sign-plates].geometryDescriptor.mergedAssembly.parts. What they are not is separate componentTree entries, because the validator counts meso components off componentTree and the generator emits one mesh per entry: three meso entries would be three more draw calls on a prop whose ceiling is two. Meeting the number literally would have meant either blowing the budget or adding empty components, and both put something in the spec that describes nothing. microFeatureGroups is met honestly at 5 localFeatures against a minimum of 3.

actionReadiness.notes: Two named parts, both individually addressable through root.userData.sculptRuntime.meshes, so the prop explodes and picks. One root pivot, no sockets, one cylinder collider on the post, no destruction groups - which matches the registry declaration exactly in both directions.

assumptions: The -Z side of both plates is plain galvanised grey with no graphic - the standard single-sided build. Confidence 0.75, from the colour of the edge return visible along the diamond's upper-right outline, which follows the diamond exactly one offset outboard and is therefore the plate's own back.

The post is a 0.075 m square hollow section. Confidence 0.80, from a single full-length vertical arris with a lit face either side and a square cut end. A U-channel is the alternative and would show a flange edge and a shadowed web.
The prop is 2.40 m tall because the registry declares it. The studio plate crops the post and shows only 1.91 m; the plate's PROPORTIONS are taken from the image and the post alone is extended.
The legend is redrawn from the known-correct string, not traced from the plate's glyphs. The reference came from a fast image model, whose Thai is approximate.
The sheeting's prismatic cell pattern is not modelled. It sits at the JPEG noise floor at 1024 and is sub-pixel at prop distance.
Fastener heads are printed, not modelled, at 0.009 m each.

componentTree.name: Sign plates (diamond warning plate + supplementary legend plate)
componentTree.topologyRationale: Decision tree step 4: hard, distinct faces you can point to and count - a front face, a back face and a constant-thickness edge wall. Folded aluminium sheet with real thickness, built as an extruded profile. NOT conforming-shell, which would mean a skin following something else's curvature with no volume of its own; NOT material-only, which has no geometry and could not show the grey edge return the reference plainly shows along the diamond's upper-right side; NOT surface-relief, since this IS the silhouette rather than detail riding on one. The grimoire's own worked example puts a flat rigid wall panel here, and its closing note says a large flat panel and a small flat plate are the same class.

geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: authored - rewritten after generation into a two-region atlas (see mergedAssembly)

mergedAssembly.reason: maxDrawCalls is 2 and this prop needs a post, so the two plates get ONE mesh between them. They are the same material, the same thickness and the same plane, so merging costs nothing in fidelity and buys the only draw call the post could otherwise not have. This is a BLOCKOUT decision, recorded here so a later pass does not 'fix' the shallow tree by splitting it and silently doubling what every instance of this sign costs a scene.

parts.note: A square on point. The profile's SHARP half-diagonal is 0.46574 rather than 0.45 because a filleted 90-degree vertex is cut back from the sharp vertex by R(sqrt2-1) = 0.01574 m, and the reference's 0.90 m was measured between the ROUNDED apexes. Built extent is therefore exactly 0.90 x 0.90.

Rounded rectangle, aspect 2.21:1 as measured. Merged into this component's buffer after generation, because THREE.Shape carries one outer contour and cannot express two disjoint islands in a single extrusion.

Not separate geometry: it IS the extrusion's side wall, 0.006 m deep, and it is what makes the plate read as folded sheet rather than a zero-thickness card. It is given the atlas's plain galvanised patch, which is why the plate's edge and back are grey while its face is yellow.

diamond-graphic.maps: the diamond plate's +Z face, local (x,y) over the 0.90 x 0.90 m bounding square

supplementary-graphic.maps: the supplementary plate's +Z face, local (x,y) over its 0.554 x 0.250 m rectangle

plain-galvanised.maps: EVERY other vertex - both plate backs and the whole edge return - collapsed to the single texel at (768, 381)

uvAtlas.rule: A vertex whose normal has z > 0.5 takes a graphic region chosen by its local y; every other vertex takes the plain patch. Collapsing the non-face vertices to one texel is what lets a single-material mesh carry a printed front and a plain back without a second material and therefore without a second draw call.
uvAtlas.note: At 569 texels per metre the diamond region already exceeds the reference itself, where the same 0.90 m spans 413 px. The atlas is built once at module scope and shared by every instance rather than rebuilt per call.

attachment.notes: The plates are embedded 0.5 mm into the post's front face rather than butted onto it. A butt joint here would be legal - the faces oppose - but the embed costs nothing and removes the question entirely.

transform.scaleNote: scale is an explicit [1,1,1] because profile2D is authored in METRES. scale_vector() prefers transform.scale over dimensions, and without it the generator would multiply the already-real profile by the dimensions again.

pivot.notes: No pivot of its own. A sign plate does not turn on anything.

actionProfile.colliderNote: Deliberately none. The declared collider is a cylinder on the POST, because what a player walks into is the post; a proxy on a plate mounted two metres up would block the pavement underneath it.

colorMaterialRecipe.notes: Three measured stops, not a ramp: the field and the margin meet as a soft gradient, the ink meets both as a hard boundary. The hard boundary is the point - a filled silhouette with a crisp edge is what survives distance and a low texture resolution.
colorMaterialRecipe.materialClassNote: plastic, not metal: the visible surface is a retroreflective vinyl/acrylic sheeting film laminated to an aluminium blank, and it is the film that light interacts with - measured metalness 0.0, a dielectric response with no specular lobe. The aluminium underneath is never seen.

localFeatures.notes: Measured 0.044 m at the left vertex and 0.031 m at the top; 0.038 adopted. Silhouette, so it must be geometry.
The 0.006 m extrusion wall. Grey, from the atlas's plain patch.

localFeatures.technique: painted decal via a generated canvas texture assigned after material construction

pictogramSource.frame: normalized unit square whose INSCRIBED DIAMOND is the black border rule's OUTER boundary; +x right, +y down
pictogramSource.note: 180-point polygon traced from the homography-rectified plate. Its normalized frame is the border rule's OUTER boundary, which is inset from the plate edge by 0.014 m perpendicular - a diamond half-diagonal shrink of 0.014*sqrt2 - so rule-frame coordinates map to plate-frame as 0.5 + (u-0.5)*0.9556.

localFeatures.notes: Rule stroke 0.020 m, edge-to-rule margin 0.014 m, both measured.

localFeatures.technique: painted decal via the same canvas
localFeatures.notes: Thai line set larger than the English line, as measured. The English line is CONDENSED: measured per-glyph advance is ~0.55 of cap height, so a normal-width face at the same size overruns the plate.

surfaceDetail.notes: bumpAmplitude is 0.0 and that is the measurement, not a gap: IQR 9 luma over the clean field.

componentTree.name: Galvanised square hollow section post
componentTree.topologyRationale: A prismatic structural section. Square rather than round on the evidence of a single vertical arris with a lit face either side of it and a square cut end; a U-channel would show a flange edge and a shadowed web, and neither is there.

geometryDescriptor.note: Kept as a plain box on purpose. The arris is the identity feature and a box already has it; adding a chamfer would spend triangles rounding off the one edge that matters.

attachment.notes: The cut end sits at y=0. Real posts continue into the ground; the prop stops at the origin.

collider.notes: The registry declares `collider: cylinder` for this asset and this is where it lands. A cylinder circumscribing a square section is the cheap convex proxy a physics engine wants; the 3 mm it adds at the corners is far below anything a player feels, and it is sized to the POST rather than to the prop so nothing blocks the pavement under the plates.

rust at the cut end, measured

seams.notes: The section's own corner. Real geometry, present in the box by construction.

materials.name: Retroreflective sign sheeting on aluminium

albedo.samplingNotes: Trimmed mean (15-85 percentile) of two crops verified clear of the border rule and the pictogram: crops/sheeting-yellow.png at (443,168,40,30) -> #D5B831 over 840 px, and a second field at (470,430,45,35) -> #CDB52F over 1102 px. No key removal was applied: the field's median luma reads 177 at the top of the plate and 173 at the bottom, so the studio gradient across the whole face is 4 luma and subtracting it would be noise, not correction. The third secondary is the algal staining, which is albedo and is carried as a localOverride.

roughness.notes: Adopted from analyze_texture.py's measured recipe for finishClass `painted-metal` on crops/sheeting-yellow.png, in preference to the 0.34 first authored by eye. The crop's specularFraction is 0.0 and its mottle is 0.035: there is no tight highlight anywhere on this face, which is a mid roughness under a soft key rather than the low one a broad sheen suggested. extract_pbr_evidence.py's 0.696 was NOT adopted - it returned 0.696 here and 0.680 for the galvanised post, two finishes that plainly differ, and two numbers that close together across two different surfaces are a class default rather than a measurement.

localOverrides.region: outboard margin of the diamond plate and along the folded edge return
localOverrides.notes: Desaturated yellow-green weathering, trimmed mean #B9AB36 over 375 green-biased pixels at (325,262,26,40). Concentrated where water sits - the outboard margin and the fold - and absent from the middle of the face. Drawn into the legend canvas as a soft margin gradient, which is where a bounded albedo region on a flat panel belongs.

localOverrides.region: border rules, pictogram and both legend lines on both plates
localOverrides.notes: Trimmed mean of the darkest half of a pictogram crop, 563 px below luma 60 at (440,285,35,35). The whole-crop mean was #2D2C20; the darker figure is the one taken because the crop's brighter half is the sheeting's ambient bounce spilling across a hard boundary, not the ink.

evidence: Measured on crop-sheeting (crops/sheeting-yellow.png, 40x30 px verified clear of the border rule and the pictogram): luma min 163, max 195, interquartile range 9. A flat field.

The faint hexagonal prismatic cell pattern visible in the yellow sits at the JPEG noise floor at 1024 and is sub-pixel at prop distance; it is recorded as undetermined in the assessment rather than modelled.

Every mark that IS on this surface - rules, pictogram, legend, algal margin - is supplied as a generated canvas texture assigned after material construction, which a procedural noise set would overwrite.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely. That function builds FIVE canvases per material at textureResolution, pixel by pixel in JavaScript with multi-octave noise, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution (256 -> 1.6 s, 512 -> 6.5 s, 1024 -> 26 s). It is also a CORRECTNESS fix: whenever a texture set exists the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding the authored albedo. reviewHistory.summary: Measured, not estimated, by the render harness: 220 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 3, one texture at 2.7 MB, and createObjectModel returning in 34 ms. DRAW CALLS are the binding axis and triangles are not - the prop sits at a quarter of its triangle budget and at 100% of its draw-call budget - and that is the design rather than an overrun, because it was decided in the BLOCKOUT and not optimised into at the end. Three splits were refused and each is recorded where someone tempted to make it will read it: the supplementary plate folds into the diamond's buffer, the plate faces do NOT get a graphic material separate from their backs, and the fasteners stay printed. The UV atlas is what makes the second of those possible - front-facing vertices take a graphic region and every other vertex collapses to a single galvanised texel, so one material carries a printed front and a plain back. NOTHING WAS DECIMATED and no segment count was cut: at 220 triangles the vertex cost is already below the per-draw-call overhead, so a decimated LOD tier would save nothing measurable and would cost a second geometry against a ceiling of three. The one place triangles WERE spent is the post's 8 height segments, 56 of them, to carry a weathering ramp that would otherwise have needed a texture. The factory was regenerated at this pass id and the post-generation layer re-applied through a recorded script, so the shipped artefact is the generator's own output plus a layer whose every part is described in the spec.

The library has no entry for hot-dip galvanised steel: material_region_analysis returned request-input at confidence 0.0 and offered aluminum, brass, copper, gold, steel-brushed and steel-polished, every one of which is model 'conductor' with metalness locked at 1.0. Weathered galvanising is an oxidised zinc layer over steel and does not behave like a clean conductor, and the reference says so: analyze_texture measures specularFraction 0.0 on the post crop, so there is no specular lobe anywhere on it, and its luma runs a gentle 115-170 gradient. A metalness of 1.0 would render a chalky post as chrome. metal.aluminum is taken as the nearest profile on its visual cues - 'bright neutral conductor, soft satin highlight unless polished' - and the shipped metalness of 0.25 is a DELIBERATE DEVIATION from its prior, evidenced above. The crop comparator passes this material at 0.8182 with the reference and render crop means within 2 per channel, so the deviation is measured, not assumed. The registry gap is a finding about the library, not about this prop.
